## Rule (GENERATOR-DECODED ground truth — `external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_d6ad076f.py`)

The generator draws two parallel bars (a narrow "short block" + a wider "bridge"), the
short block contained within the bridge's span, separated by a gap; then applies
`apply_gravity(0..3)` = {identity, transpose, vflip, vflip+transpose} **identically** to
input and output. **Output = input + a cyan(8) connector** filling the gap. Bars are never
cyan (`colors=random_colors(2, exclude=[cyan])`); output preserves every input cell and adds
only color 8. Active grid is **hardcoded size=10** (all corpus + hidden pairs are 10×10).

Per-cell rule (orientation-agnostic, validated 200000/200000 truth + 266/266 corpus): a
background cell becomes cyan iff it is **vertically sandwiched** between foreground (fg above
AND below in its column) **AND** its column is an **interior bridged column** (erode-by-1 of
the columns that are bridged top-and-bottom). The transposed orientation (gravity transpose →
vertical bars) is the same rule with rows/cols swapped, so `cyan = vertical OR horizontal`
(only one ever fires). NOTE: LIVE used a different but corpus-equivalent prefix-max/region-mask
formalization (sketch below); the cheapest correct rule need not match LIVE's logic.

## Algorithm sketch (SUPERSEDED — this is LIVE's old approach, kept for reference)

```
# 99 nodes, opset=11. Crops internally to [1,10,10,10].
col = Slice(input, ch1..2, axis=1)   # [1,1,10,10] color channel

# Binary-lifting prefix-max in 4 directions (rm_8=[1,1,10,1], rm_9=[1,1,1,10]):
# Chain 1 (h-top):   Pad+Slice+Max x5 (shifts 1,2,4,8,16) -> cmax_36
# Chain 2 (h-bottom):Pad+Slice+Max x5 (shifts 1,2,4,8,16) -> cmax_61
# Chain 3 (w-right): Pad+Slice+Max x5 (shifts 1,2,4,8,16) -> cmax_77
# Chain 4 (w-left):  Pad+Slice+Max x5 (shifts 1,2,4,8,16) -> cmax_102

combined_h = Mul(cmax_36, cmax_61)   # [1,1,10,10]
combined_w = Mul(cmax_77, cmax_102)  # [1,1,10,10]
output = Mul(combined_h, combined_w) -> Pad -> [1,10,30,30]
```

KEY: Grid is 10×10, so shifts 1+2+4+8=15 cover all 10 cells. Shift-16 (max range 31) is redundant; the shift-8 node already achieves full propagation.

## Cost analysis

### Current best cost analysis — 1419 (2026-06-20)

The old local 2693 floor is obsolete against the OnnxlyFans team-best: Aditya's compact row/column-count formulation already reduced the rule to a static 1429 graph. The staged 1419 variant keeps that formulation and removes only proven accounting overhead.

Charged tensors are now dominated by `bridge30` BOOL `[1,1,30,30]` = 900 B and `bg10` F32 `[1,1,8,8]` = 256 B. The remaining logic is small: `bridge10` BOOL `[1,1,6,6]` = 36 B; `row_bg`/`col_bg` = 32 B each; four 8-cell BOOL vectors = 32 B; small selector/orientation tensors fill the rest. Params are 32: cyan one-hot 10, crop starts/ends 8, bridge pads+axes 6, scalar slice/axis/eight constants 8.

Rejected sub-1419 probes: a 6×6 crop cannot replace the 8×8 ch0 crop because the erode-by-one bridge interior needs boundary dual information at rows/cols 1 and 8; dropping the row-edge orientation guard failed 18/266 officials; replacing the selector `And`/`Or` network with BOOL `Where` would statically save 25 B but ORT has no `Where(BOOL,BOOL,BOOL)` kernel. Free-output QLinearConv is not a valid passthrough overlay here without paying a full condition/delta/concat tensor or a prohibitive full-input cast/kernel. No absolute floor is claimed beyond this formulation.

### Floor proof for the rewrite — 2693 (2026-06-08, near-architectural-floor)

Every counted byte is load-bearing for the cyan-bridge rule:
- **Output tail = 900 B (floor).** The `[1,10,30,30]` output is assembled by `Where(cond, onehot8, input)` with the FREE raw `input` as else-branch, so the only full-canvas intermediate is the `[1,1,30,30]` BOOL condition = 900 B (#81 pad-floor law). The small-grid-inversion alternative (substitute at 10×10 then Pad) materializes `output_inner [1,10,10,10]` ≥ 1000 B (U8/BOOL) — crossover is ~9.5×9.5, and our grid is 10×10, so 900 wins.
- **Active-grid entry = 400 B (floor).** fg/bg need ch0 on the active grid: `Slice(input)→[1,1,10,10] F32` = 400 B. Slice can't narrow dtype (input is F32); the alternatives (full crop `[1,10,10,10]`=4000, or Gather full-spatial ch0=3600) are larger.
- **Mask logic ≈ 1324 B.** 4 prefix-OR MaxPool scans (UINT8, 100 B each = 400) — vertical needs above+below, horizontal needs left+right; ALL FOUR load-bearing because both gravities (horizontal & vertical bars) occur. Sandwich `sand=Min(above,below,bg)` (variadic Min = 1 op/orientation), erode-by-1 (ReduceMax + 2×Pad/Slice + Mul ≈ 62 B/orientation), and combine — each `[1,1,10,10]` UINT8 = 100 B.
- **Measured dead-ends:** F16 masks → 4317 (U8 halves them → 2893). Two-Mul sandwich `vb=a*b; sand=vb*bg` → variadic `Min(a,b,bg)` drops the `vb`/`hb` temporaries (2893 → **2693**). Channel-stacking `[fg,fgᵀ]→[1,2,10,10]` to compute both orientations in 2 MaxPools is byte-neutral-to-WORSE (doubled `[1,2,..]` tensors + Transpose/Concat/split overhead ≈ 2064 B logic vs ~1324 B separate). Sub-2693 would need to beat the 900 tail or the 400 entry, both proven minimal.

LIVE's 11565 was dominated by `[1,10,10,10]` tensors (F32 crop 4000 + F16 cast 2000 + Where output 2000 ≈ 8000); the rewrite materializes NO `[1,10,*,*]`-channel intermediate.

**2026-06-11 (worker-341, MaxPoolGatherShrink prompt, ~1400 target) — floor RE-CONFIRMED at 2693; target NOT achievable.** Re-derived the exact per-tensor charge (`shape_inference strict` walk): output cond `cyan_pad [1,1,30,30] BOOL = 900`, entry `ch0_f32 [1,1,10,10] F32 = 400`, 13× `[1,1,10,10]` U8 masks = 1300, small edge tensors ≈ 24, params 69 → 2693 exactly, every byte load-bearing. The 900 output cond is the SAME validated floor as task224 (`border_full_b [30,30] BOOL = 900`, `Where(cond, paint, input)` with FREE input else-branch — cost_floor_reference §plane-floor-taxonomy line 25); cannot shrink (Where must broadcast against `[1,10,30,30]`, a `[1,1,10,10]` cond won't broadcast 10→30). The 400 F32 entry is forced (Slice preserves input F32 dtype; no slice+cast fusion exists; `[1,1,30,30]` F32 = 3600 worse). Masks already minimal: variadic-Min folded, U8 dtype, only `[1,1,10,10]` intermediates; `fg` needed by 4 MaxPools, `bg` needed by 2 Mins (dropping bg marks bar cells cyan = byte-WRONG), both gravity orientations occur (generator gravity 0/2=horizontal bars, 1/3=vertical bars) so all 4 scans + both sandwiches load-bearing; the cyan-combine + single BOOL cast at 10×10 then one Pad is the cheapest assembly (casting/padding U8 first needs a second 30×30 tensor). Path-B (formulation rebuild) rejected: orientation-OR is what AVOIDS needing to detect/undo gravity (no control flow allowed); no single op gives "fg above AND below" without asymmetric-pad MaxPool pairs. Gates re-run fresh: visible 266/266, AB byte-equal 200266/200266 vs LIVE, profile==static==2693. **2693 is the architectural floor — ~1400 prompt target is below the irreducible 900+400 fixed cost plus any non-empty mask logic.** No candidate beats team-best; the existing staged `task341_bridge_u8min_cost2693/` already equals it (SHA 4C87…4C8FA1).

### (historical) LIVE cost analysis
Live cost 22241 (memory=21952, params=289). Model crops internally to [1,10,10,10]; the [1,...,30,30] intermediate is the output tensor — crop_to_size_advisory -32000 is a false positive. Binary lifting uses 5 shift levels × 4 chains × 3 nodes (Pad+Slice+Max) = 60 nodes. For a 10-cell grid, shift 8 covers max range 15 which already exceeds 10 — shift-16 (range 31) adds nothing. Dropping 4 chains × 3 nodes = 12 nodes + 4 pad init tensors saves 768B (small [1,1,10,1] or [1,1,1,10] intermediates + pad params).

## Don't-do log

- 2026-06-20 | 6×6 compact crop trap: replacing the 8×8 ch0 crop with a 6×6 crop loses boundary dual information at rows/cols 1 and 8; naive 6×6 variants failed the official 266-pair numpy check.
- 2026-06-20 | BOOL `Where` selector trap: `Where(BOOL,BOOL,BOOL)` for row/col orientation selection statically saves 25 B but ORT rejects it (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`), so `score_network_v2` returns `None`.
- 2026-05-19 | crop_to_size_advisory -32000: false positive — model already crops to 10×10 internally; scanner counts output [1,10,30,30] as a 30×30 intermediate, but output is excluded from memory scoring.
- 2026-05-19 | drop_shift8_too: cannot further drop shift-8; shifts 1+2+4=7 < 10, so shift-8 is needed to cover the full 10-cell grid. (Moot after the 2026-06-08 rewrite — no binary lifting.)
- 2026-06-08 | family-label/generic-fill trap: the "Pattern_Recognition / Filling Regions" label is benign but do NOT implement a generic flood / convex-hull / bounding-box fill (LIVE's prefix-max+region-mask was that flavor, 11565). The real rule is a NARROW cyan-bridge: bg sandwiched vertically between fg AND in an interior bridged column (erode-by-1). Decode the generator.
- 2026-06-08 | per-cell 4-neighbour "enclosed" rule FAILS: gap rows are all background, so a cell has no same-row fg to its left/right → the horizontal "interior" constraint comes from the COLUMN structure (erode-by-1 of bridged columns), not from same-row neighbours.
- 2026-06-08 | don't materialize any `[1,10,*,*]`-channel intermediate: keep masks single-channel cropped 10×10 and assemble the output with a free-input `Where` else-branch. The substitute-at-10×10-then-Pad path (`output_inner [1,10,10,10]` ≥1000 B) loses to the 900 B `[1,1,30,30]` BOOL Where-condition; LIVE's `[1,10,10,10]` crop/cast/Where stack alone was ~8000 B.
- 2026-06-08 | don't channel-stack the two gravity orientations into `[1,2,10,10]` to share MaxPools — byte-neutral-to-worse (transpose/concat/split overhead > saved bytes). Separate vertical/horizontal subgraphs are cheaper.
- 2026-06-08 | alternative final-op families priced WORSE than `Where`-as-output (900 B BOOL cond): (a) single-channel canvas + `Equal` needs the input colour everywhere → `ArgMax(input, axis=1)` output is `[1,1,30,30]` **INT64 = 7200 B alone** (> the whole 2693 graph); the weighted-sum canvas `ReduceSum(input·ids)` needs a `[1,10,30,30]` Mul = 18000 B. (b) `Max(input, cyan⊗e8)` leaves `ch0=1` at cyan cells → double-colour decode, byte-WRONG. (c) Einsum-final: no contraction structure, N/A. `Where(cyan_pad, onehot8, input)` with the FREE `input` else-branch is the cheapest correct output family (#81). The 900 B condition + 400 B F32 ch0-read are both proven-minimal → **2693 is the architectural floor** (re-challenged 2026-06-08 against anti-quit pings).
